summary: Edo Shonin works in religious and Buddhist studies, having earned a PhD from Nottingham Trent University. In 2015, they were attested as a research psychologist at Nottingham Trent University and Research Director at the Awake to Wisdom Centre.

Edoardo Siani works in Buddhist and religious studies, completing an M.A. in Social Anthropology at SOAS (2014-2018). He held posts at Kyoto University (2018-2020), SOAS (2018-2019), and became an assistant professor at Ca' Foscari University of Venice in 2020.

Indologist and linguist Edouard Müller-Hess studied at Tübingen, Humboldt University of Berlin, and Leipzig (Ph.D. ~1873-1874). He taught German at Cardiff University (1883-1888) and served at the University of Bern as PD (1881-1883) and Professor of Sanskrit (1888).

Linguist Eduard Buschmann studied at Berlin under Franz Bopp, Göttingen, and Königsberg (Hon. Ph.D. 1835). He worked at the Royal Library of Berlin from 1832, the Prussian Academy of Sciences from 1851, and Humboldt University of Berlin (~1840-1880).

Linguist Eduard Böhmer studied at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg (~1847-1851). He later held posts at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg (1859-1872) and the University of Strasbourg (~1872-1879).

Sinologist Eduard Erkes studied at the University of Leipzig (~1910-1913) under August Conrady, whom he later succeeded. He held long-term posts at the University of Leipzig (~1917-1958) and Humboldt University of Berlin (~1947-1958).

Linguist and Indologist Eduard Hermann studied at Freiburg, Leipzig, and Jena (Ph.D. under Berthold Delbrück). He held professorships at Kiel (1913), Frankfurt (1914), and Göttingen (1917-1937), where he succeeded Jacob Wackernagel.

Eduard Müller was a scholar in Indology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics. He completed his inaugural dissertation at the University of Leipzig (~1873-1874) and served as a professor at the University of Bern (~1886-1907).

Linguist Eduard Prokosch studied at Charles University, Vienna, Chicago, and Leipzig (Ph.D. ~1904-1905). He taught at Wisconsin-Madison (1905-1913), Texas at Austin (1913-1919), Bryn Mawr College (1919-1928), and Yale University as Sterling Professor (1929).

Indologist and philosopher Eduard Röer studied under Johann Friedrich Herbart and Franz Bopp, earning a Ph.D. at Berlin. He was PD in Berlin (1833-1838) before working for the Asiatic Society, Bibliotheca Indica, and the East India Company.

Eduard Sachau studied linguistics and Iranian/Central Asian studies at Kiel, Leipzig, and Halle (Ph.D. ~1867) under Nöldeke, Brockhaus, and Fleischer. He served as professor at Vienna (1869) and Berlin (1876), also directing the Seminar für Orientalische Sprachen (1887).

Linguist and Indologist Eduard Schwyzer studied at Zurich (PhD under Adolf Kaegi) and Leipzig. He held professorships at the University of Zurich (1909, 1912), University of Bonn (1927), and Humboldt University of Berlin (1932-1939).

Linguist Eduard Sievers studied at Leipzig and Berlin under Friedrich Zarncke, Georg Curtius, and August Leskien. He held professorships at the universities of Jena (1871-1883), Tübingen (1883-1887), Halle-Wittenberg (1887-1892), and Leipzig (1892-1922).

Indologist Eduard Thommen studied at the University of Basel (~1899-1901), the University of Paris, the University of Oxford, and the University of Göttingen, where he completed his PhD (~1901-1903) under Jacob Wackernagel.

Linguist Eduard Wölfflin studied at the University of Basel (~1849-1851) and the University of Göttingen (~1851-1854). He held posts at the University of Zurich (~1869-1871), University of Erlangen-Nuremberg (~1871-1880), and University of Munich (~1880-1905).

Eduard Zeller was a philosopher and religious studies scholar who studied at the Tübinger Stift and University of Tübingen (~1831-1836). He held posts at Tübingen, Bern, Marburg, Heidelberg, and Humboldt University of Berlin (~1872-1895).

Eduardo Francisco Freyre Roach is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a Master of Buddhist Studies at the University of Hong Kong (attested 2014) under the supervision of Yakupitiyage Karunadasa and Georgios T. Halkias.

Eduardo Luigi De Stefani worked in linguistics and Indology, having studied under Paolo Emilio Pavolini (~1895-1898). In 1910, he held a teaching post in Latin and Greek grammar at Sapienza University of Rome.
Indologist and linguist Edvard Brandes studied at the University of Copenhagen under Niels Ludvig Westergaard, earning an M.A. in Oriental Philology (~1865-1872) and a Ph.D. (~1872-1879).

Edvard Westermarck worked in philosophy and religious studies after studying at the University of Helsinki (~1881-1889). He later held academic posts at the London School of Economics (~1904-1930) and Åbo Akademi University (~1918-1932).
